title: Vertex count along a surviving trace
statement: Let $T$ be a surviving trace of length $\mathrm{steps}$ over a vertex type $\alpha$: a family of states $(G_j, C_j)$ indexed by $j \in \bbn$, in which each consecutive pair below $\mathrm{steps}$ is joined by a surviving step (the graph $G_{j+1}$ arises from $G_j$ by contracting an edge that does not cross the distinguished cut). Then for every index $i \le \mathrm{steps}$, the number of vertices of the graph at index $i$ equals the number of vertices of the initial graph at index $0$ minus $i$; that is, $\lvert V(G_i)\rvert = \lvert V(G_0)\rvert - i$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a surviving trace of length steps
index i is at most steps
replaced:
For $i \le \text{steps}$, the graph at index $i$ of a surviving trace has vertex count
equal to the initial vertex count minus $i$.
